question: Which of the following options is correctly paired?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria – Membrane-bound.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria – Membrane-bound is correctly paired.**
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles present in all **eukaryotic cells' cytoplasm.**
 
• Typically it is sausage-shaped or cylindrical having a **diameter of 0.2-1.0μm (average 0.5μm) and a length of 1.0-4.1μm.**
 
• Each mitochondrion** is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner membrane **dividing its lumen distinctly into two aqueous compartments, i.e. the outer compartment and the inner compartment.
 
• The inner compartment is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called **the matrix.**
 
• The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary of the organelle.
 
• The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called **the cristae.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosomes:**

 
 
• These are membranous granular structures present in the cytoplasm.
 
• They were first observed under an electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade in the year 1953.
 
• Ribosomes are the site for** "protein synthesis" so they are also called the "protein factory" **of the cell.
 
 
 
• **The nucleus:**
 
 
• It is a pivotal organelle responsible to regulate almost all forms of cellular activities.
 
• Mostly, every type of cell that exists is categorized on the basis of the absence or presence of the nucleus within its cell (categorized either as a prokaryotic or eukaryotic cell).
 
 
 
• **Plastids:**
 
 
• These are responsible for photosynthesis, storage of products like starch, and for the synthesis of many classes of molecules such as fatty acids and terpenes, which are needed as cellular building blocks and/or for the function of the plant.
